item.title: 49ers game grades: Potent offense outscores fierce Cowboys comeback attempt
item.description: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Deebo Samuel Sr. and guard Dominick Puni celebrate a touchdown against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas. (Icon Sportswire/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) The San Francisco 49ers raised their record to an NFC-best 8-1 in the offensive showcase everyone expected, going up against the Cowboys in Dallas. The Niners scored 46 points on six touchdowns in their win , getting a personal record performance from Brock Purdy , and showing a readiness to fend off a ferocious Cowboys rally. Offense: A Expectations that Sunday would be a track meet were certainly met by the offense. Christian McCaffrey busted out for 223 total yards and three touchdowns on 17 touches, Deebo Samuel added 109 and two more scores, and Kaelon Black added a sixth trip to the end zone with 66 yards on 13 touches. Purdy's 389 passing yards were a career high, while passing for three touchdowns (two to McCaffrey, one to Samuel) despite getting sacked five times. In addition to getting Samuel back in action, new wideout Keenan Allen made five catches on seven targets in his Niners debut. Defense: D+ About that track meet, yeah, the defense held up its end as well, surrendering 40 points while registering just one sack and one turnover (Malik Mustapha's interception) and allowing 439 yards and letting Dallas score on all three of its red-zone opportunities. That said, there were moments where the defense almost made a big difference that hinted at the unit's potential at full strength; they registered 10 hits on Cowboys QB Dak Prescott, Dre Greenlaw almost made a second-quarter interception on a play where Nick Bosa was in Prescott's face and Fred Warner - who led the team with 11 tackles - forced what looked like a late-game fumble that ultimately wasn't called. Special teams: B As much as this might be a "do no harm" area during a week where the opposing offenses were trading haymakers, the important news is that Eddy Piñeiro didn't miss a kick, making all five extra-point attempts and his lone field-goal attempt. But added credit to Samuel for recovering the inevitable onside kick attempt with 43 seconds left after Dallas narrowed affairs to a single score, and to punter Corliss Waitman for burying the Cowboys on their own 9-yard line on his kick with just 21 seconds left. This was the kind of game where those things mattered. Coaching: B+ Kyle Shanahan 's offense was certainly ready to exploit the Cowboys' porous defense and show it has some big-play ability at any age, while Raheem Morris' defense delivered a fairly respectable game until giving up three fourth-quarter touchdowns. Unfortunately, it still wasn’t enough as the Cowboys lost a 46-40 shootout to the NFC-leading Niners . The Cowboys scored three touchdowns in the fourth quarter, including one by Lamb with less than a minute left in the game, to make the score a bit more respectable. The Seattle Seahawks started the season slowly with three losses in their first six games, but it appears the defending Super Bowl champions are getting close to hitting their stride again. The Seahawks picked up their second consecutive victory and improved their record to 6-4 with their 21-13 triumph over the Las Vegas Raiders. Never in 6A Texas football in the Metroplex, never at Ohio State in his 347-yard Rose Bowl, not in the NFL has Jaxon Smith-Njigba said he’s had a quarter like the third today here in Las Vegas. Oh, and about that OPI that negated his TD in the 1st half today @933KJR pic.twitter.com/J659czF7gi Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Gregg Bell (@gbellseattle) November 16, 2026 The Seahawks ruined the first start of Las Vegas rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza, who took over as the Raiders’ starting quarterback after Las Vegas traded previous starter Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings hours before the trade deadline Tuesday. The Seahawks were led by backup QB Drew Lock and superstar wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Lock played in place of QB1 Sam Darnold and he was razor sharp. He completed 14 of 17 passes for 240 yards with 2 TD passes. One of those scoring throws was to Smith-Njigba while the other was to Cooper Kupp. Smith-Njigba led the Seahawks with eight catches for 171 yards. item.title: Cris Collinsworth says Bengals' fans are noticing Tee Higgins limping
item.description: Cincinnati Bengals receiver Tee Higgins was injured during the second quarter of the team's NFL Week 10 showdown with the Pittsburgh Steelers on NBC's Sunday Night Football at Paycor Stadium. Higgins grabbed his leg after a catch, and went to the sideline. He limped noticeably after an incompletion shortly before halftime, but stayed in the game and had a 14-yard catch on the next play. "He has been limping a little bit, and I'm sure Bengals' fans are paying attention," NBC analyst Cris Collinsworth said during the broadcast. Higgins celebrated the 50th TD catch of his NFL career by handing the ball to an excited young fan during the team's NFL Week 9 win against Atlanta. Higgins helped teammate Ja'Marr Chase celebrate his touchdown with a nod to Spanish bullfighting . Higgins was named AFC Offensive Player of the Week for his effort in Cincinnati's 43-36 overtime win in NFL Week 8 against Tennessee. It was Higgins' first career AFC Offensive Player of the Week award. Higgins had 10 catches for 155 receiving yards against the Titans, and caught two of quarterback Joe Burrow's five touchdown passes . After being held without a catch during the first half, Higgins went off during the second half of a Week 7 rout in Baltimore, catching six Joe Burrow passes for 148 receiving yards with a touchdown. Earlier in the second half, Higgins' shoulder and arm were evaluated by medical personnel after he absorbed a big hit from Ravens defensive back Kyle Hamilton after a catch. Before the bye week, Higgins was dealing with an adductor injury he suffered in a Week 4 loss to Jacksonville. Against the Jaguars, Higgins got up slowly after a 19-yard catch near the sideline from Burrow . Higgins got up, but then took a knee. Higgins returned to the game later in the drive, and made a catch on his first play back in the game. He was not on the field for the Bengals' final drive of the game. Higgins had a game-high 10 catches for 140 receiving yards before the injury. He added a 17-yard catch, giving him a total of 157 receiving yards, second only to the 194-yard game he had against Baltimore in 2021. Higgins made a remarkable touchdown catch from quarterback Burrow late in the second quarter of the team's Week 3 loss to Pittsburgh at Acrisure Stadium. It was among the most impressive NFL catches by Higgins . In March 2025, Higgins agreed to a four-year contract extension with the team. Higgins, Cincinnati's second-round pick in the 2020 NFL draft, is entering his seventh NFL season. item.description: San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper (2) reacts to making a 3-point basket during the second half of an NBA basketball game against the Utah Jazz, Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in Salt Lake City. (AP Photo/Tyler Tate) (Tyler Tate/Associated Press) With the lowly Utah Jazz threatening to put an end to the Spurs' 12-game winning streak in the fourth quarter Sunday, one thought when through Dylan Harper's mind. "It's time to take over," the Spurs guard said. "It's time to win." Done and done. Harper scored 18 of his career-best 31 points in the final frame to help the Spurs stave off the spirited Jazz 110-102 at the Delta Center. With the victory, the Spurs (12-2) clinched their longest winning streak since 2015-16. They won 11 in a row on two occasions last season. Victor Wembanyama scored 21 of his 26 points in the first half, adding 10 rebounds, six assists and five blocks to the winning effort. Stephon Castle chipped in 20 points and nine assists, while Keldon Johnson muscled his way to an 11-point, 10-rebound double-double off the bench. On paper, Utah hardly looked like the team to give the Spurs' latest winning streak a scare. The Jazz entered Sunday having lost 11 in a row, every bit as cold as the Spurs have been hot. Utah was once again without its All-Star frontcourt of Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. Jusuf Nurkic and Jaxson Hayes were also sidelined, leaving Mo Bamba to make his first start since April 2025 with Orlando. San Antonio Spurs forward Victor Wembanyama dunks during the first half of an NBA basketball game against the Utah Jazz, Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in Salt Lake City. (AP Photo/Tyler Tate) (Tyler Tate/Associated Press) Bamba, who had not attempted a 3-pointer this season before Sunday, went 6-of-6 from beyond the arc on his way to 26 points. He was 10 of 13 from the field. Rookie guard Darryn Peterson added 17 points, and the Jazz found themselves with a four-point lead with 5:25 remaining. That's when Harper decided he had seen enough. The 20-year-old became the fifth player in Spurs history to record a 30-point game before his 21st birthday, joining Tony Parker, Jeremy Sochan, Wembanyama and Castle. Harper made six of his eight shots in the fourth quarter and all four of his free throws, repeatedly answering the Jazz whenever they threatened to pull away. His 3-pointer from the left wing brought the Spurs within 98-97 with 3:18 to play. After Bamba's dunk restored Utah's three-point cushion, Harper answered with another 3, this one from the right wing, to tie the game. The Spurs never trailed again, escaping with a victory that kept their winning streak intact. item.title: Steelers safety Jaquan Brisker motivated by his late brother
item.description: When we went to talk with Jaquan Brisker in the locker room after their Week 1 win against the Falcons, Channel 11 Sports Director Jenna Harner noticed a T-shirt hanging in his locker with a picture of a young Gateway football player wearing No. 3. We learned it’s his older brother, Tale, who died when Jaquan was just 15 years old. In a raw and open conversation, Brisker shared with Harner how much of an impact Tale had on his life, and why his older brother is one of the main reasons he’s here today. It’s hard to put into words just how much Brisker looks up to his older brother. Growing up, the two were inseparable. “We all thought we was rock stars,” Brisker said. “So all of us, we had this camera. ... We would do all these videos. We were in a rap group or whatever and just be singing different things, dancing and stuff like that. They also played a lot of sports, from football to basketball, roughhoused even more. Tale, who was four years older, always made sure to take his younger brother under his wing. “What was your relationship like just the two of you?” Harner asked. “Yeah, it was amazing,” Brisker said. “‘Cause to be honest, I was in the shadow. I was always shy and things like that. And he was the one to bring me out that comfort zone. But on an early February day in 2015, Brisker’s world was forever changed. He was at a lift, and was confused when his family tried to call him during school. When he arrived at his coach’s house where he was staying, his dad’s car was outside. “When I see him, the first thing I thought, I literally said to him, I’m like, oh, I’m like ‘(Expletive) something’s going on. Something’s wrong,’” Brisker said. Tale was shot and killed in his apartment in Prairie View, Texas. He was just 19 years old. “I remember taking the dog out and then just breaking down crying right there,” Brisker said. “And then I think I probably cried that whole trip to my aunt. And then walked in, hugged my aunt. And then my mom was upstairs. Everybody was torn apart.” “What was the hardest part for you after he passed?” Harner asked. “The toughest part is hearing my mom cry the whole time, and yeah, that was tough. That was tough the whole time,” Brisker said. The last conversation he had with his older brother is one Brisker will never forget. Tale told Jaquan that if anyone in the family was going to make it, it would be him. “Obviously he was telling me to be smart, know, stay in school, you know, just follow in the right direction, things like that,” Brisker said. “And then he knew I love football so much ‘cause obviously we always talked and I always thought my brothers would make it to the NFL, things like that. item.title: CBF mourns the passing of Dino Sani, 1958 World Cup winner
item.description: CBF mourns the passing of Dino Sani, 1958 World Cup winner Dino Sani, a 1958 World Cup winner, has died at 94 Credits: CBF The Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF) deeply mourns the passing of Dino Sani, the former midfielder and 1958 World Cup winner, who died this Sunday (15) at the age of 94. He was part of the first Brazil team to take the country to the pinnacle of world football. “We have lost one of our first world champions. Dino Sani etched his name into the history of the Brazilian national team in 1958. His name will forever stand among the greats of the Amarelinha. At this difficult time for his family and friends, I offer my condolences and pay tribute to this great champion and idol,” said CBF president Samir Xaud. Dino played 24 matches for Brazil, recording 16 wins, four draws and four defeats. He scored four goals. At the 1958 World Cup, he played in the first two matches, against Austria (a 3–0 win) and England (a goalless draw). A muscle injury then ruled him out of the rest of the tournament, and Zito took his place. In addition to the World Cup, he helped win the Oswaldo Cruz Cup (1958), the Bernardo O'Higgins Cup (1959) and the Roca Cup (1960). 1958_06_08_Brazil 3–0 Austria_STANDING De Sordi, Dino Sani, Bellini, Nilton Santos, Orlando, Gilmar. item.title: Louisville Crushes #4 UConn 69-51
item.description: Louisville has a veteran-heavy team and when you have returning players it’s easy to compare them to seasons past. Last year the Cards could jump out to big leads but it often seemed like they’d fold in the 3rd quarter. Tonight Louisville withstood every run, kept their foot on the gas, and dominated the Huskies the entire game in front of a crowd of 12, 692. Imari Berry led all scorers with 21 points. Tajianna Roberts had 11 points but more interestingly she also had 8 rebounds. Both Zamareya Jones and Mackenly Randolph had 10 points and 9 rebounds respectively. Tajianna Roberts said, “In the huddle we kept saying that it’s 0-0 and to not play the score. Take it one play at a time. We weren’t worried about how much we were up. We knew they were capable of making runs so we were just playing as if it was 0-0.” She added, “We stayed composed. I think we’ve learned as vets now as Juniors.” Imari Berry added, “We believed in each other. We came back and we knew what we needed to do and I feel like we’re standing on business.” Coach Walz was impressed with his team’s play especially in rebounding. “I was really proud of the way we competed from start to finish. We talked to everybody about the importance of rebounding the basketball. It was going to take the entire team we can’t just rely on E [Elif Istanbulluoglu] or Mack. It takes everybody. I thought it’s the best effort we’ve had top to bottom.” He added, “Zam and Taj rebounding the basketball were elite. We only gave up 7 offensive boards. They missed 40 shots— 21 of 61 from the field— and we only gave up 7 offensive boards. That’s as good as it gets.” He talked about the importance of getting Mackenly and Elif back after injuries. “Mack and E are our 2 most important players on our team. Hands down. And it’s not because they’re going to score 20. It’s because they communicate and they talk the entire time… They’re directing everybody and they might not always get the credit but they’re why defensively we were as good as we were.” He also praised Imari, “It’s what Imari does. She’s special. She’s a kid who’s continued to work on her game we knew this coming out of high school but it was just a matter of getting her to believe how good she really is. I’m not sure she really understands how good she is…. What you’ve seen through the first 6 games is what we saw all summer long.” Statement win ‼️ #GoCards pic.twitter.com/flm9JRRZOP — Louisville Women’s Basketball (@LouisvilleWBB) November 16, 2026 The Cards turn around and play another home game this Tuesday against Tennessee State. item.title: Collinsworth slams Jordan Battle for Bengals-Steelers taunting penalty
item.description: NBC Sports analyst and former Cincinnati Bengals receiver Cris Collinsworth blasted defensive back Jordan Battle for his unsportsmanlike conduct/ taunting penalty during the second quarter of the NFL Week 10 game between the Bengals and the Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium on NBC's Sunday Night Football . Battle stood over Steelers receiver DK Metcalf after breaking up an Aaron Rodgers pass to Metcalf. "He just sat there and looked at him and cost his team 15 yards, and gave the Steelers a chance to wake up," Collinsworth said of Battle's penalty during the broadcast. Battle was limited during the week before the Bengals' Week 9 win against Atlanta in Spain because of a hamstring injury. The NFL announced a fine of $21,623 for Battle for unnecessary roughness (use of the helmet) during the Bengals' Week 5 win in Miami . Battle was limited during the week before the Bengals' loss to Jacksonville because of a hamstring injury. Battle, a third-round pick of the Bengals in the 2023 NFL Draft out of Alabama, is in his fourth NFL season with Cincinnati. He played in all 51 of the Bengals' games over his first three seasons, recording six interceptions and making 30 starts. On his 25th birthday , Battle had an interception of Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson during the second quarter of the Cincinnati's NFL Week 15 loss . Battle was injured during the fourth quarter of the Bengals' Week 13 loss to Pittsburgh last season. During the 2024 season, Battle recovered a fumble and returned it during the third quarter of the Bengals' NFL Week 15 win against Tennessee, but Battle lost the ball just shy of the goal line through the back of the end zone for a touchback. item.title: St. Charles falls in OHSAA Division I boys soccer state final
item.description: Another deep tournament run ended in unfortunately familiar fashion for the St. Charles soccer team. The Cardinals almost tripled Kettering Fairmont in shots and earned a handful of quality scoring chances in the Division I boys state final Nov. 15 at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field, but the first-time state finalist Firebirds converted a higher percentage of opportunities and came away with a 3-1 win. Senior forward Sam Lofthouse scored St. Charles’ only goal, spinning and shooting from about 25 yards to the right of the goal with 25:35 to play and sneaking his shot into the upper right corner. That made it 2-1, but Fairmont (15-5-3) got the goal back less than four minutes later. Gavin Weaver’s corner kick got all the way through traffic, and Luke Davidson put it in from right in front. Azariyah Nsabimama and Aaron Black scored 12 minutes apart in the first half for Fairmont, and St. Charles lost for only the fourth time this season (18-4-1) and first since its regular-season finale Oct. 15 against Worthington Kilbourne. St. Charles, appearing in its 12th state tournament, fourth in a row and seeking its first title since 1985, outshot Fairmont 23-8. The Cardinals also were state runners-up in 2024, 2016, 1991, 1988 and 1981. St. Charles had outscored its first five tournament opponents 15-3, including a 1-0 win over defending state champion Dublin Jerome in a state semifinal in which Lofthouse had the only goal. Cardinals sophomore goalie Micah Neil made three saves. Fairmont’s Carson Dewald stopped six shots. This story will be updated. item.title: 'You live for them, you play for them' - Auston Trusty honors late father with goal on emotional USMNT return
item.description: Auston Trusty GFX - GOAL In his first match since his father’s death, Auston Trusty scored against Haiti and found comfort in the teammates he calls family. The goal was only part of the story. MIAMI -- For one brief moment, Auston Trusty's sadness subsided, and his competitiveness took over. As he ran towards the corner flag after scoring his second U.S. Men's National Team goal, Trusty got caught up in the moment. He cupped his hands and stared at the crowd full of Haitian fans just seconds after giving his side a 1-0 lead. And then, as he ran back to his spot on the field, he remembered. The goal faded and reality set in. As happy as he was with his finish, Trusty was still adjusting to a new reality, one without the man he looked up to most. Saturday’s game was Trusty’s first since his father, Walt, passed away on Oct. 19. The weeks since have been difficult, to say the least. Celtic granted him time away to grieve, and he joined USMNT camp directly after attending his father’s funeral. Saturday marked his return to competitive action. It was fitting, then, that Trusty was the first USMNT player to find a moment of joy against Haiti. It didn't fix anything, and it won't, but Trusty's early goal brought peace and comfort to a man who has spent the last few weeks searching for just that. "I'm just honored to represent him," Trusty said postgame, "and play with his last name and showcase for him. I want to showcase to the world what I can do for him and his glory. I'm just very proud to score today and have a good game." Even in a 6-0 win where goals blend, Trusty's goal stood out. It was, as he said, a tribute to something bigger. More specifically, it was a tribute to someone who meant so much to him. A difficult time Unless you’ve experienced it, it’s hard to grasp the emotional toll of losing a parent. Trusty has spent the past few weeks grappling with that loss alongside his family in Pennsylvania. Walt Trusty, like his son, was a standout athlete. Back home in Media, Pa., he was a history-making basketball player in the late 60s and early 70s. As his playing days ended, his fandom remained, as he supported the local Philadelphia teams. More importantly, he also supported his children. He had six of them, and Auston was his youngest. As Trusty blossomed as a soccer star, first locally and then in Europe, the centerback's father was there every step of the way. Just this summer, he was able to watch on as his son played in, and scored in, a World Cup. item.title: David Adelman Frustrated Nuggets Didn't Shoot the Ball More in Win over Pelicans
item.description: On Saturday night, the Denver Nuggets defeated the New Orleans Pelicans 116-108. The Nuggets were on a four-game road trip, and this was the last game of their stretch. The Nuggets were led by Jamal Murray , who had 23 points, and, Nikola Jokic, who had 26. Overall, this was a full team effort from Denver, and this game was interesting because the Nuggets barely shot the ball from three-point range. Denver shot 4-of-16 from three in this game, and after the game, head coach David Adelman wished his team had shot the ball more from long range. Matthew Hinton-Imagn Images “I thought in the first half we would turn down a great shot and then end up with an okay shot at the end of the shot clock,” Adelman said . “I’d like to see guys be more confident, shoot the thing. It just leads to more flow, it leads offensive rebounding.” Denver getting a win like this has to be encouraging for this coaching staff. In recent seasons, the Nuggets have been known to be a team that is capable of spreading the floor at a high level, but this shows they can dominate in the interior as well. Denver had 62 points in the paint, a very impressive effort from a team that usually shoots the ball more often than not. Matthew Hinton-Imagn Images The Nuggets’ emphasis on scoring inside is encouraging, and if this team can continue to play like that in the interior, it will make them more dynamic. Jamal Murray has been playing really well from the perimeter so far this season, and if the rest of the team can follow suit, it will continue to open things up for them on offense. What has made the Nuggets so dangerous over the years is their spacing. David Adelman could be right in asking his squad to continue to shoot the ball, as it has been part of their identity. With this win, the Nuggets moved to 7-4 and were 3-1 throughout their road trip. They have also been winners of four of their last five games, and it seems like they’re starting to build some consistency this season. Matthew Hinton-Imagn Images Coming into this season, they were hoping their veteran presence would be the reason they could outmatch teams in the NBA, and it has helped them in certain games. It will be interesting to see how they approach their next game offensively and whether they will prioritize shooting the ball from a distance more.
